objects.description: Tag type used to request in-place construction of contained objects (polyfill for std::in_place_t when C++17 is unavailable).
Exception type base specialization for void, thrown/reported on invalid expected access when exceptions are enabled or used for traits otherwise.
Tag type to request in-place construction of the error state of expected.
Policy struct providing how to rethrow or handle stored errors when accessing expected::value() on an error state. Specialized for exception_ptr and error_code.

functions.name: nonstd::in_place
functions.signature:
template<class T>
nonstd::in_place_t in_place(nonstd::detail::in_place_type_tag<T> = nonstd::detail::in_place_type_tag<T>())
functions.description: Returns a nonstd::in_place_t tag for in-place construction by type. Primarily used in pre-C++17 builds to emulate std::in_place_type. Passively returns a tag; overload selected by the template parameter T.
requirements: T may be any type; there are no runtime constraints.
This is a tag-returning utility; it does not construct objects itself.

functions.description: Returns a nonstd::in_place_t tag specifically for in-place construction of a value of type T. Provided for pre-C++17 compatibility.
requirements: T may be any type; there are no runtime constraints.
This is a tag-returning utility; it does not construct objects itself.

functions.name: nonstd::make_unexpected
functions.signature:
template<typename E>
constexpr auto make_unexpected(E&& value) -> nonstd::unexpected< typename std::decay<E>::type >
functions.description: Factory function that constructs and returns a nonstd::unexpected holding an error value of type decay<E>. This is the branch used when the header is configured to use std::expected; the alias unexpected_type maps to std::unexpected.
requirements: E must be a type that can be decay-copied/moved into unexpected<decay<E>>.
The argument value is forwarded to the unexpected constructor.

functions.name: nonstd::expected_lite::swap
functions.signature:
template<typename E
    , typename = typename std::enable_if< nonstd::expected_lite::std17::is_swappable<E>::value >::type>
void swap(nonstd::unexpected_type<E>& x, nonstd::unexpected_type<E>& y) noexcept(noexcept(x.swap(y)))
functions.description: Swaps the contained error values of two unexpected_type<E> objects. Delegates to unexpected_type<E>::swap.
requirements: E must be swappable (std17::is_swappable<E>::value).
The operation is noexcept if E is nothrow swappable.

functions.name: nonstd::expected_lite::swap
functions.signature:
template<typename T, typename E
    , typename = typename std::enable_if< (std::is_void<T>::value || std::is_move_constructible<T>::value) && std::is_move_constructible<E>::value && nonstd::expected_lite::std17::is_swappable<T>::value && nonstd::expected_lite::std17::is_swappable<E>::value >::type>
void swap(nonstd::expected_lite::expected<T,E>& x, nonstd::expected_lite::expected<T,E>& y) noexcept(noexcept(x.swap(y)))
functions.description: Swaps two expected<T,E> objects. It calls x.swap(y), which exchanges either the held values or errors, or moves between value/error states as needed.
requirements: T must be void or move-constructible.
E must be move-constructible.
T and E must be swappable (std17::is_swappable<T> and std17::is_swappable<E>).
The operation is noexcept if T and E are nothrow move-constructible and nothrow swappable as used by expected::swap.

functions.name: nonstd::expected_lite::operator==
functions.signature:
template<typename E1, typename E2>
constexpr bool operator==(nonstd::unexpected_type<E1> const& x, nonstd::unexpected_type<E2> const& y)
functions.description: Compares two unexpected_type objects for equality by comparing their contained error values (x.error() == y.error()).
requirements: E1 and E2 must support operator== on their contained error types.

functions.name: nonstd::expected_lite::operator==
functions.signature:
template<typename T1, typename E1, typename T2, typename E2
    , typename = typename std::enable_if< !std::is_void<T1>::value && !std::is_void<T2>::value >::type>
constexpr bool operator==(nonstd::expected_lite::expected<T1,E1> const& x, nonstd::expected_lite::expected<T2,E2> const& y)
functions.description: Equality comparison between two expected objects with non-void value types. Returns false if their states differ; otherwise compares contained values (*x == *y) or errors (x.error() == y.error()).
requirements: T1 and T2 must not be void.
If both have values, T1 and T2’s value types must be equality comparable.
If both hold errors, E1 and E2 must be equality comparable.

functions.name: nonstd::expected_lite::operator!=

functions.description: Inequality comparison for unexpected_type. Returns !(x == y).
requirements: E1 and E2 must support operator== on their contained error types.

functions.name: nonstd::expected_lite::operator!=

functions.description: Inequality comparison between two expected objects. Defined as !(x == y).
requirements: The corresponding operator== overload must be valid for the involved T/E types.

functions.name: nonstd::expected_lite::make_unexpected_from_current_exception
functions.signature: nonstd::unexpected_type<std::exception_ptr> nonstd::expected_lite::make_unexpected_from_current_exception()

functions.name: nonstd::expected_lite::make_expected_from_error

constexpr nonstd::expected<T, typename std::decay<E>::type> nonstd::expected_lite::make_expected_from_error(E e)
functions.description: Factory that creates an expected<T, decayed<E>> containing an unexpected constructed from the provided error value e.
requirements: Enabled only when nsel_P0323R <= 3 (compile-time configuration).
E must be decays-to a type usable as error_type and be copy/move constructible into unexpected_type.

functions.name: nonstd::expected_lite::make_expected_from_call
functions.description: Invokes f() and returns expected<R> with the returned value on success; on exception, returns unexpected_type<std::exception_ptr> captured from the current exception. Overload for non-void return.
requirements: Enabled only when nsel_P0323R <= 3 (compile-time configuration).
SFINAE: enabled only if std::result_of<F()>::type is not void.
f must be callable as f() with no arguments.
If f() throws, the exception is caught and converted via std::current_exception().
